question: What happens to the current if I raise the resistance in a circuit?

frames.data: data: {"type":"probe","id":"current-used-up","question":"A cell is connected in series to two identical bulbs, one after the other. How does the current just before the first bulb compare with the current just after the second bulb?","options":["The current after the second bulb is smaller, because the bulbs use some of it up.","The current is the same at both points, because the bulbs transfer energy but do not use up current.","The current after the second bulb is zero, because the bulbs use all of it."],"correct":1,"explanation":"Charge is not used up, so the current is the same at every point in a series circuit. What the bulbs take from the circuit is energy, which they give out as light and heat.","basis":"This correction is the assistant's own wording of a standard idea.
